# RETRO: #12750 follow-up (team 4)

## What worked
- One neutral brief with read-only snapshots (head, prior, merge base) gave both reviewers identical scope; both reached the same disposition independently.
- Opus's neutralized real-command differential (1168 argvs) was a strong regression check for a router change.

## Process deviations
- Coordinator: the Sol exit check tailed `receipts/sol-wait-1.stdout`, and that output included Sol's one-line summary before Opus finished. Nothing was disclosed to Opus. Fix: `pi_job.py wait` should print only state/exit to the caller, or coordinators should redirect it and read only `.exit`.
- Coordinator: `git clone` exit 128 was a `cat-file` probe on missing PR commits (default clone lacks PR refs), not a clone failure; fixed by fetching `pull/12750/head`. Brief should always name the PR ref fetch.
- Opus: wrote `full-router.diff` briefly to the session scratchpad and then moved it into `opus/scratch`; used three parallel 50-line reads per response (over the 60-line aggregate); two `cut -c` reads of its own summary (not presented as complete). Disclosed in its report.
- Sol: used the shared clone at `28ceaae` only as review.py's required source carrier; executed routers were copies of the pinned exports. Disclosed.

## Tooling notes
- Feature request: `pi_job.py wait` summary should omit `latest_text` to protect independence.
- `comment-requirements.md` "Current model preference" still says "Opus 5.5 High" while the runtime table defaults to xhigh; the requirements snapshot needed an applicability note.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Follow-up on [the earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12750#issuecomment-5788206253), checked at `d2a4222`.** The earlier finding, "PATH-only commands can override existing checkout aliases", is **resolved**. No new issue was found in the changed router code.

**Verified:** As described in [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12750#issuecomment-5789613981), the PATH lookup now runs at the end of [`dispatch_or_help`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/d2a422283d8f71ef5903586117fc8ddea5235a6d/bin/omarchy#L1090-L1121), after metadata routes, group help and prefix help, just before the unknown-command error. With the same **synthetic** colliding PATH-only stubs as before:

| Existing checkout route | Additional PATH-only executable | `2308791` | `d2a4222` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shot x`, alias of `omarchy-capture-shot` | `omarchy-shot` | PATH command | Checkout alias, as on baseline |
| `finalize thing`, metadata route of `omarchy-provision-thing` | `omarchy-finalize` | PATH command | Checkout command, as on baseline |
| `grp`, group containing `omarchy-grp-a` | `omarchy-grp` | PATH command executes | Group help, as on baseline |

Group `--help`, alias `--help`, a metadata-only group and prefix help also match baseline output with colliding PATH entries present.

**Verified:** The original fix still works in a simulated package layout. `omarchy debug --no-sudo --print` reaches the PATH-only command. `debug --help` and `debug --help --json` render metadata without executing it. `upload log` without its required argument shows help. Unknown commands still exit 127 with the same suggestion text. For all shipped commands with neutralized bodies, output matched the previous revision in both a checkout layout and a package layout.

**Verified:** The full `test/cli` suite passes at `d2a4222` (119 `ok` lines). Run against the `2308791` router, the new alias test fails, and the new group test fails on its own when the alias test is removed.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Head `d2a4222`, compared with `2308791` and the merge base; isolated router tests with synthetic executables and real command metadata, plus the full `test/cli` suite. Actual package installation and diagnostic collection were not exercised.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis; independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments of this revision; Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check of presentation and privacy, not technical correctness.
